newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECHS PLAN FOR EU ENTRY TALKS TO START BY MID-'98.
newsitem.headline: CZECHS PLAN FOR EU ENTRY TALKS TO START BY MID-'98.

text.p: The Czech government is aiming to have its strategy for European Union accession ready by early to mid-1998 when membership talks are expected to begin, a senior government adviser said on Monday.

"We have between 13 and 16 months to define our negotiation positions, to create the team of negotiators, including the main negotiator," Jan Zahradil an adviser to Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus told a news conference.

Speaking after a meeting of a government committee on European integration, Zahradil said that the main task for the Czechs in preparing for EU membership was to bring more laws and regulations in line with those of the Union.

The EU has said it would open expansion talks with prospective new members about six months after the end of its intergovernmental review conference, currently underway, which is expected to conclude by the middle of next year.
Diplomats have repeatedly listed the Czechs among top candidates from the former East Bloc for early EU entry.

Ahead of the Czechs' formal application to join the EU, which was submitted last January, Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus said it was "realistic" that his quickly-reforming economy would be accpeted by the end of the century.
He has since backed off that comment, and has declined to estimate when the country might be a full member.
Zahradil declined to list possible officials who might lead the Czech negotiating team.
He said by the end of the century, the Czechs must reconsider another 200 legal norms which differ from EU standards. He declined to say what regulations were still problematic.
In July, the Czech cabinet approved responses to a 1,100-point EU questionaire for would-be members from the former East Bloc.
The EU sent the questionnaire to all associate members seeking full membership asking for detailed information on their political, economic and social situation.
